title: Heaps and Priority Queues
summary: Keep the smallest or largest item available without keeping the whole collection sorted.
keyPoints: A min-heap keeps the smallest item at the root; a max-heap keeps the largest.
Push and pop are O(log n); peek is O(1).
A heap is a complete binary tree stored in an array, so it needs no node objects.
A size-k heap is the standard way to find the top k items in O(n log k) time.

complexity.note: The root is always the extreme.
Bubble up from the last slot.
Move the last item to the root, bubble down.

complexity.operation: Build a heap from n items

commonMistakes: Sorting the whole input when only the top k items are needed.
Using the wrong heap direction: a min-heap of size k keeps the k largest values, with the smallest of them on top.
Forgetting that Python's `heapq` is a min-heap, so max-heap problems need negated values.
Mutating an item already inside a heap without reheapifying it.
interviewNotes: Say why a heap is better than sorting: O(n log k) versus O(n log n) when k is much smaller than n.
For merging k sorted lists, put the head of each list in a min-heap and pop the smallest repeatedly.
For scheduling, clarify whether the heap stores start times, end times, or remaining work.

checkYourself.question: Why does a size-k min-heap give the k largest values?
checkYourself.answer: Keep the heap at size k. When a new value is larger than the smallest value in the heap, replace that smallest value. The heap ends up holding the k largest values seen.

checkYourself.question: Why is building a heap O(n) rather than O(n log n)?
checkYourself.answer: Bottom-up heapify performs less work for most nodes. The total number of swaps is bounded by a constant times n.

checkYourself.question: How do you merge k sorted arrays with a heap?
checkYourself.answer: Put the first value from each array into a min-heap with its array index. Pop the smallest, append it, and push the next value from that same array.
